What we do

Four rights every child is owed

Our partners work across all four, from a safe birth to a voice in the village council.

Survival

A healthy start for every child

Malnutrition, missed vaccines and unsafe births still threaten children’s survival in the poorest communities, especially in their first five years.

  • Growth monitoring and nutrition support for young children
  • Immunization drives with community health workers
  • Clean water, sanitation and hygiene in homes and schools
Health & nutrition
Development

Every child in school, learning

Too many children start school late, drop out early or sit in classrooms without learning to read. Girls are the first to be pulled out when money is short.

  • Enrolling out-of-school children and keeping them in class
  • Extra teaching so children read and count at grade level
  • Bridge courses that bring girls back into the right grade
Child education Girl-child education
Protection

Childhoods free from work and early marriage

Millions of children work in fields, homes and workshops instead of going to school, and child marriage still ends many girls’ education.

  • Finding working children and bringing them back to school
  • Community vigilance to stop child marriages before they happen
  • Village child protection committees
Child labor Child marriage
Participation

A voice in the decisions that shape their lives

When children speak up in their schools and villages, problems get noticed sooner and solutions last longer.

  • Children’s and girls’ collectives that meet, learn and speak up
  • Children taking part in school management committees
  • Young people raising issues with local officials
